headline: Massachusetts closes shellfish beds statewide ahead of nor’easter
dek: The precautionary order takes effect before sunrise and bars harvesting from Massachusetts waters until the Division of Marine Fisheries reopens the areas.
body: Massachusetts has ordered all shellfish-growing areas statewide closed as a precaution ahead of the nor’easter, prohibiting people from harvesting or attempting to harvest shellfish from state waters.

The Division of Marine Fisheries said the closure begins a half-hour before sunrise on Saturday, Sept. 26, and will remain in place until the agency changes the areas back to open status. The affected waters extend along the Massachusetts coast from the New Hampshire line to the Rhode Island line and include the state’s listed shellfish-growing management areas.

The order also prohibits possession of shellfish taken from Massachusetts waters during the closure. Aquaculture permit holders may not harvest or remove shellfish from growing sites for culling while the restriction is active. The advisory excludes conch and sea scallop adductor muscle from the closure.

The agency cited forecast high winds, coastal flooding and heavy rainfall from the storm. Coastal communities including Chatham, Eastham and Yarmouth repeated the advisory in local notices and told residents and harvesters to check the Division of Marine Fisheries for reopening information before returning to the flats.
author: NorthEast News Desk
